title: Session 1: Coordinating Conjunctions: FANBOYS
summary: The four types of conjunctions, then full mastery of the seven FANBOYS: what each one means, when to use it, and exactly when to put a comma before it.

blocks.title: By the end of this session you can …
items: Name the four types of conjunctions and give an example of each
Use each FANBOYS conjunction with the right meaning
Put a comma before FANBOYS only when it joins two independent clauses
Use nor correctly (nor + auxiliary + subject)

blocks.text: A **conjunction** is a joining word. It links words, phrases or clauses and shows how the ideas are related. In this course we study all four types, one by one:

rows: joins two equal parts: two words, two phrases or two independent clauses
for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so
joins a dependent clause to an independent clause
either … or, neither … nor, not only … but also
link two independent clauses or two sentences (with ; or a full stop)

blocks.title: Key words you need today
items: **Clause** = a group of words with a **subject + verb**: the bus arrived.
**Independent clause (IC)** = a clause that makes sense on its own as a sentence: The bus arrived.
Session 5 goes deeper into clauses. For today, remember: **subject + verb = clause**.

blocks.text: The first letters of the seven coordinating conjunctions spell **FANBOYS**: **F**or · **A**nd · **N**or · **B**ut · **O**r · **Y**et · **S**o.

rows: We stayed inside, **for** it was raining heavily.
addition, or one action after another
Omar finished his essay, **and** he checked it carefully.
Laila did not finish her homework, **nor** did she revise for the test.
The test was long, **but** it was not difficult.
You can write a letter, **or** you can send an email.
He studied for hours, **yet** he failed the test.
The library was closed, **so** we studied at home.

blocks.title: FOR = because (gives the reason)
items: The clause **after** for is the reason: The farmers were worried, **for** there had been no rain.
For is formal. It only joins two independent clauses, so there is **always a comma before it**.
It cannot start the sentence with this meaning: ✗ For it was cold, we lit a fire. ✓ We lit a fire, for it was cold.

blocks.title: AND = addition or sequence
items: Adds one more fact: The city is crowded, **and** the air is polluted.
Shows one action after another: She opened the letter, **and** her face went pale.
Don't chain many clauses with and (I woke up and I ate and I left and …). Use different conjunctions instead.

blocks.title: NOR = and not (a second negative)
items: The first clause is negative (not, never, no). Nor adds another negative idea.
After nor, the word order changes: **nor + auxiliary + subject + verb**.
He cannot swim, **nor can he** ride a bike. · They did not apologise, **nor did they** explain. · She is not ready, **nor is** her brother.
✗ She didn't call, nor she texted. ✓ She didn't call, nor did she text.

blocks.title: BUT = contrast
items: Joins two ideas that are different or opposite: The phone is expensive, **but** it is reliable.
Never use but and however together: ✗ but however.

blocks.title: OR = choice, alternative or warning
items: Choice: We can take the train, **or** we can drive.
Warning (= otherwise): Leave now, **or** you will miss the bus.
In a negative sentence, or joins the items: I don't drink tea **or** coffee.

blocks.title: YET = surprising contrast
items: Like but, but the second idea is **unexpected**: The road was icy, **yet** he drove fast.
But = simple contrast. Yet = "and this is surprising".

blocks.title: SO = result
items: The clause **before** so is the cause; the clause **after** so is the result: It was late, **so** we took a taxi.
Don't use because and so in the same sentence: ✗ Because it was late, so we took a taxi.
So that (= purpose) is a different conjunction. We study it in Session 2.

blocks.title: FOR vs SO: same facts, opposite direction
items: It was late, **so** we took a taxi. → cause first, result after so.
We took a taxi, **for** it was late. → result first, reason after for.

blocks.text: This is the most important rule of today. Look at what comes **after** the conjunction.

rows: two **independent clauses** (new subject + verb after the conjunction)
Sara opened the book, **and she** started reading.
Sara opened the book **and started** reading.
tea **and** coffee · short **but** clear · at home **or** at school
three or more items in a list
We need pens, paper and a ruler.

blocks.title: The 3-second test
items: Cover everything before the conjunction. Read what comes after it.
Does it have its **own subject + verb** and make sense alone? → **IC, FANBOYS IC** (comma).
No subject? → **no comma**.

blocks.title: Three mistakes to avoid
items: **Comma splice:** two independent clauses joined by a comma only. ✗ It was raining, we stayed inside. ✓ It was raining, so we stayed inside.
**Comma after the conjunction:** ✗ It was late but, we waited. ✓ It was late, but we waited.
**Comma between two verbs:** ✗ Ali finished the test, and left. ✓ Ali finished the test and left.

blocks.title: Academic writing tip
items: In formal academic writing, avoid starting a sentence with And, But or So.
Join the two clauses with **comma + FANBOYS**, or use a conjunctive adverb such as However or Therefore (Session 4).

items.q: Choose the best FANBOYS: I wanted to go to the match, ___ I had too much homework.
Choose the best FANBOYS: The shop was closed, ___ we went home.
Choose the best FANBOYS: She was very tired, ___ she kept working until midnight.
Choose the best FANBOYS: He didn't eat breakfast, ___ did he eat lunch.
Choose the best FANBOYS: We must leave now, ___ we will miss the train.
Choose the best FANBOYS: The old man smiled, ___ he had finally found his son.
Comma or no comma? Mona wrote the report and sent it to her teacher.
items.a: **No comma** — sent has no new subject (two verbs, one subject).

items.q: Comma or no comma? Mona wrote the report and her teacher marked it.
items.a: **Comma**: Mona wrote the report, and her teacher marked it. (new subject her teacher + verb marked)

items.q: Comma or no comma? Do you prefer maths or science?
Correct the mistake: The film was boring, I left early.
items.a: Comma splice. ✓ The film was boring, so I left early.

items.q: Join with **for**: She wore a coat. It was freezing outside.
items.a: She wore a coat, for it was freezing outside.

items.q: Rewrite using **so**: We cancelled the trip, for the weather was terrible.
items.a: The weather was terrible, so we cancelled the trip.

items.q: Join with **nor**: He did not say sorry. He did not offer to help.
items.a: He did not say sorry, nor did he offer to help.

blocks.title: Session 1 Practice Quiz
blocks.intro: 15 questions. Choose the best answer. You see your score and the explanations at the end.

questions.q: How many coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS) are there?

questions.e: for = because; so gives the result.

questions.q: The test was hard, ___ everyone passed. Which shows a surprising contrast?
You should wear a helmet, ___ you could get hurt.
He didn't study, ___ did he attend the review session.

c: I was hungry so, I made a sandwich.
I was hungry, so I made a sandwich.
I was hungry, so, I made a sandwich.
I was hungry so I, made a sandwich.
Karim locked the door and went to bed.
Karim locked the door, and went to bed.
Karim locked the door and, went to bed.
Karim, locked the door and went to bed.
questions.e: Two verbs, one subject → no comma.

questions.q: Which sentence needs a comma before the conjunction?
c: The bell rang and the students left the room.
She sang and danced all night.
questions.e: the students left = new subject + verb → IC, and IC.

questions.q: She did not phone, nor ___ an email.

c: The sun set, and the sky turned red.
The sun set and turned the sky red.
As the sun set, the sky turned red.
The sun set, the sky turned red.
The road was closed so, we went back.
So the road was closed, we went back.
The road was closed, so we went back.
Because the road was closed, so we went back.
because of bad weather, we stayed.

questions.q: In formal academic writing, which is the best choice?
c: But the results were not clear.
The results were interesting. But they were not clear.
The results were interesting but, they were not clear.
The results were interesting, but they were not clear.

questions.q: Which pair shows the **same facts** correctly?
c: It rained, yet we stayed in. / We stayed in, or it rained.
It rained, for we stayed in. / We stayed in, so it rained.
It rained, so we stayed in. / It rained, for we stayed in.
It rained, so we stayed in. / We stayed in, for it rained.
